messages.subject: different chains don't agree
parts:
Dear Stan Users,
I am running 4 chains, each with 10,000 steps. When I plot the lp__ of these chains, I found that they are quite flat within the chains, but differ a lot between different chains. I don't quite understand why that happens, and if I want the chains to converge, should I increase the number of chains or the number of steps or anything else?

Thanks,
Jingjing

messages.author: f53f4ca2c430170d
messages.subject: Re: different chains don't agree
parts:
On Monday, July 18, 2016 at 6:24:02 PM UTC-4, Jingjing Chen wrote:
Dear Stan Users,
I am running 4 chains, each with 10,000 steps. When I plot the lp__ of these chains, I found that they are quite flat within the chains, but differ a lot between different chains. I don't quite understand why that happens, and if I want the chains to converge, should I increase the number of chains or the number of steps or anything else?

This is pretty straightforward.  Your model is defining a posterior with multiple modes. The modes are too widely separated (with too deep a valley between them) for the sampler to traverse back and forth so you are not getting convergence (the chains are sampling from different parts of the posterior and you don't get much indication of which part is more important).  This is related to having multiple local optima in optimization but with the added complication that an MCMC sampler can often explore multiple modes so if it is failing to do so the multiple modes are clearly well separated.  Why it's hapenning I can't tell without seeing the model but the typical culprits are mixture models, heavy tailed distributions, particularly for poorly observed parameters, ..., sorry can't come up with the full list but those are the ones I run into most commonly.

Krzysztof

 

Thanks,
Jingjing

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: different chains don't agree
parts:
I disagree--maybe.  Slow convergence does not have to be coming from multiple modes.  It could be slow convergence within a single mode.
A
